name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,242

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sea getting at other times called on for fish

blocks.note: the Med is the usual short name for the Mediterranean Sea
aka, 'also known as', introduces another name a thing goes by

explanation.surface: A sea creature that keeps changing its name on the fishmonger's board.
explanation.definitionFit: The medaka is a small Japanese freshwater rice fish, widely kept in aquariums and laboratories.

clue.text: Aussie howler upset visiting Brit? What a week!

indicators.note: in a down entry, something upset is turned upside down, so the word it governs reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: Australians call a British visitor or immigrant a Pom
eh is a startled 'what?'
taken as written
the standard abbreviation of week

explanation.surface: An Australian complains loudly about a whingeing British visitor and the dreadful week they have had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Howler' suggests a blunder, but here it is a creature with a cry. MOPEHAWK is a variant name of the mopoke, an Australian owl named for its call.
explanation.definitionFit: The mopehawk is the Australian boobook owl, a night bird famous for its repeated hooting call.

clue.text: Old rag added to waiter’s tips

indicators.note: tips are the far ends, so only the final letter of each word is wanted

blocks.note: the closing letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An old cloth is thrown in with the gratuities a waiter collects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' looks like a scrap of cloth, but here it is the verb meaning to tease; DOR is an obsolete word for mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To dor was an archaic verb meaning to mock, make fun of or play a trick upon someone.

clue.text: What Finn plucks from leaping deer impaled on stake

indicators.note: a leaping animal is all over the place, so its letters jump into new positions
something impaled has a spike driven through it, so one word goes right inside the other

blocks.note: the elk is a large deer
the ante is the stake put up before a hand of poker

explanation.surface: A grisly hunting scene of a deer speared on a post, apparently explaining where a Finn gets something to pluck.
explanation.definitionFit: The kantele is the traditional plucked zither of Finland, the national folk instrument of the Kalevala.

clue.text: Drug swallowed, now losing weight: I’m laughing!

indicators.note: losing means something is dropped from the word before it

blocks.note: past tense of eat
taken as written
W abbreviates weight; it is the letter dropped
LOL is text-speak for laughing out loud

explanation.surface: Someone who has taken a slimming pill finds the weight falling off and laughs with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Atenolol is a beta-blocker medicine prescribed for high blood pressure and angina.

clue.text: Indian city’s current police, once welcome, blame everyone in it after rising

indicators.note: in places everything before it inside the last word
in a down entry rising means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001
a friendly greeting
to take the rap is to take the blame
all people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city's history: its police force of old, once friendly, now blames everybody after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of five pieces goes inside IT once that word has been turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiruchirappalli, often called Trichy, is a large city in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

clue.text: Bright colour cheers one handy with paint tin up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the pieces read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks
an RA is a Royal Academician, a distinguished painter
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A decorator raises a tin of paint in a toast to a vivid new shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacarat is a bright orange-red shade, also the name of fabric dyed that vivid hue.

clue.text: Rare stone is indulgence after changing hands over an evening, informally

indicators.note: changing hands swaps right for left, so one R letter becomes L

blocks.note: a luxury is an indulgence
the indefinite article
nite is the casual spelling of night

explanation.surface: A precious stone changes hands one evening as a casual treat.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L stand for right and left, so the hand change turns LUXURY into LUXULY; 'over' puts it above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxulyanite is a rare tourmaline-bearing granite from Luxulyan in Cornwall, used for the Duke of Wellington's sarcophagus.

clue.text: Old chest or “box” used by speaker, not unknown around area

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the following item out
around says the shortened word wraps itself about the next piece

blocks.note: the voice box
y is an algebraic unknown; it is the letter removed
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An ancient trunk, or a speaker's box, with something unknown inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint that 'box' is figurative: the voice box.
explanation.definitionFit: A larnax is an ancient Greek or Minoan chest or coffin, often of terracotta and used for burials.

clue.text: Back rooms requiring work: one’s nonetheless to be suitable for lawgiver

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
one is I, and the 's stays as S
informal short form of though
as in 'that will do'
Moses brought the Ten Commandments down from Sinai

explanation.surface: Rear rooms needing renovation are still declared fit for a great legislator.
explanation.definitionFit: Opisthodomoi are the rear chambers of Greek temples, behind the main cella, often used as treasuries.

clue.text: Dad managed pub in Morecambe, perhaps, close to vital waste filtering facility

definitions.text: close to vital waste filtering facility

indicators.note: in places the pub inside the name that follows

blocks.note: familiar word for father
ran a business is managed it
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, so his first name is one example
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Father ran a pub in the Lancashire seaside town of Morecambe, near the sewage works.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe reads as the resort town, but it stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranephric means situated beside the kidney, the organ that filters waste from the blood.

clue.text: Circuit of Doone country, missing odd parts

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters go missing, leaving the second, fourth and sixth

blocks.note: Lorna Doone, R D Blackmore's novel, is set on Exmoor, moorland in south-west England

explanation.surface: A tour of the moorland made famous by a romantic novel, skipping the odd bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuit' sounds like a walk round, but it is an electronic one.
explanation.definitionFit: An XOR, or exclusive-or gate, is a logic circuit whose output is true when exactly one input is true.

clue.text: Is one who’s permitted initially satellite dishes with lights?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word only

blocks.note: read as 'one who has let': who's stands for who has, and to let is to permit
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A query about whether a licensed person can mount illuminated satellite dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Lights are the lungs of a slaughtered animal, a classic ingredient of offal dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Haslet is a meatloaf or roast of pig's offal, traditionally including the heart, liver and lungs.

clue.text: Crack heard every so often under small wooden sleeper in Victoria

indicators.note: every so often takes only alternate letters of the word

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
made of pine, a common timber
to have a crack or a bash is to make an attempt
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Something cracks under a little wooden railway sleeper at a Victorian station.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria suggests the London station and its railway sleepers, but it is the Australian state; 'under' puts the second half below the first in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a spine-basher is an idler or loafer who spends time lying on their back.

clue.text: Ring within ring, close to anther elsewhere?

definitions.text: Ring within ring, close to anther elsewhere?

indicators.note: within puts the first ring inside the second
elsewhere says a letter leaves its usual place in the word and goes somewhere else
close to means the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: a collar is a ring round the neck
its final letter
the letter shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A botanist describing whorls of a flower, one ring inside another, near the pollen-bearing anther.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the petals form a ring inside the ring of sepals, next to the anthers. The closing letter of the neck ring shifts to a new spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The corolla is the ring of petals in a flower, lying inside the ring of sepals and next to the stamens.

clue.text: A number from Berlin recycled which Stasi term (it is Wehrmacht’s, also)?

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A query about which Cold War secret police term came out of Berlin, with a Nazi army aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin suggests the German city, with the Stasi and Wehrmacht to match, but it is the songwriter Irving Berlin. The bracket is a bonus: it is Wehrmacht's also gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote the song White Christmas, made famous by Bing Crosby, so it is one of his numbers.

clue.text: Old friar’s touching prayer, second about to be forgotten

indicators.note: something to be forgotten is dropped and left out of the word

blocks.note: re means concerning or touching on
a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy
c. for circa means about; it is the second C that goes

explanation.surface: An elderly friar's moving prayer, a moment's thought before it is forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' reads as moving, but it means regarding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Recollets were a reformed branch of the Franciscan order, founded in France in the late sixteenth century.

clue.text: German engineer, old one in shock, before long becoming calmer

indicators.note: in puts the one inside the word for shock

blocks.note: Karl Benz built the first practical motor car
standard abbreviation
a daze is a stunned state
Roman numeral
to pine for is to long for

explanation.surface: An elderly German engineer in shock gradually becomes calmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calmer' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: something that calms.
explanation.definitionFit: Benzodiazepines such as Valium are sedative drugs prescribed to calm anxiety and aid sleep.

clue.text: Old-fashioned clowning to go with some butting in

indicators.note: butting in means pushing into the middle of something

blocks.note: go and zing both mean energy or zest
as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Slapstick of the old school involves a lot of headbutting.
explanation.definitionFit: To zany was an archaic verb for playing the buffoon, so zanying is acting the clown.

clue.text: Mostly being just low grades for class fluent in Latin?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

blocks.note: equity is fairness, the quality of being just
E is a low mark in exams, so two of them

explanation.surface: A school report complains that a Latin class earns poor marks despite being fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a school group, but it is a social rank in ancient Rome, where everyone spoke Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The equites were the Roman knights, the equestrian order ranking just below the senators in Roman society.

clue.text: No longer trusted, if deaf to reform

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are remade in another order

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is no longer believed when they claim to be deaf in order to change their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' reads as a loss of trust, but it marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Affied is an obsolete past participle meaning confided in or relied upon, from the old verb affy.

clue.text: One gives support to organ, not to Scottish miners

blocks.note: frae is Scots for from, the opposite of to
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers

explanation.surface: A church benefactor backs the organ fund, not one for Scottish coal miners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a church instrument, but it is the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraenum is a small fold of tissue, like the one under the tongue, that anchors and restrains an organ.

clue.text: Jealous, with last letter being the very last, and after a Scrabble tile!

indicators.text: with last letter being the very last
indicators.note: the word's last letter is swapped for the last letter of the alphabet
a scrabble is a frantic scramble, so the letters get mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player is jealous because an opponent got the Z tile to play last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' looks like the board game, with its tiles, but it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An azulejo is a glazed and painted ceramic tile, typically blue and white, found across Portugal and Spain.

clue.text: Make more of Shakespeare, less of dramatic heroines

indicators.note: less of means only a small portion of the words that follow is taken

blocks.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A director gives the Bard more prominence and the leading ladies less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of Shakespeare' marks the word as one Shakespeare used.
explanation.definitionFit: Ich is a Shakespearean form of eke, meaning to augment or increase, as in King Lear.

clue.text: One leading different parties, all on the same side

indicators.note: different means changed, so the words after it appear in another order

blocks.note: Roman numeral
ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician heads several parties at once while insisting they are all on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipsilateral is an anatomical term for structures or symptoms located on one and the same half of the body.

clue.text: Auditor’s rank that’s used for a spell in Greece

definitions.text: that’s used for a spell in Greece

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so we want the word as it is heard

blocks.note: a rank is a row or line

explanation.surface: An accountant's grade, used for a stint working in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, and 'spell' a period of time, but one is a listener and the other is spelling words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet, one of the letters used to spell Greek words.

clue.text: State control, shadowy, about to tamper with lives

indicators.note: about means the word for shadowy goes around what follows

blocks.note: dim and shadowy both mean poorly lit
to rig is to tamper with
is, as in exists

explanation.surface: Shady state control is on the point of meddling with people's lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the wrapping signal and 'to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirigism, from French dirigisme, is an economic doctrine in which the government directs industry and investment.

clue.text: When very dry, becoming drunk?

definitions.note: the answer is the old adjective, besotted; 'drunk' is used figuratively

blocks.note: as in 'as I was leaving'
so much is very much
TT, teetotal, describes someone who does not drink

explanation.surface: A paradox: getting drunk while being completely teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'drunk' as figurative: intoxicated with love, not alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Assott is a Spenserian word for infatuated or besotted, which is being figuratively intoxicated.
